question.text: Kolar Gold Fund (Cat II, 5-yr): Committed Capital INR 100 cr. Year 2 NAV pre-incentive = INR 105 cr. Year 2 HWM (prior year NAV pre-incentive) = INR 102 cr. Year 2 Reference Hurdle NAV (Year 2) = INR 121 cr. Incentive Fee rate 15%. Under the 'higher of HWM and Reference Hurdle' rule illustrated in the chapter, what Incentive Fee is the Manager eligible for in Year 2?

explanation.text: The Logic: Applicable benchmark (not eligible for incentive) = HIGHER of HWM and Reference Hurdle = max(INR 102 cr, INR 121 cr) = INR 121 cr. NAV pre-incentive = INR 105 cr < INR 121 cr. Since NAV is BELOW the applicable benchmark, incentive fee = ZERO. This replicates the chapter's Worst-Case Scenario (Example 6.4). The Trap: A ignores hurdle and uses HWM only (wrong — take HIGHER of the two); C uses hurdle but wrongly generates a positive (nav is actually below hurdle); D is absurd. Cross-Exam Context: Chapter 6 Worst-Case Example 6.4. Note: HWM appears here as a Cat I/II safeguard at DEAL-by-deal exits — not a Cat III daily crystallisation. XIX-E tests the Cat III variant. Manager's Pro-Tip: Even though HWM is primarily Cat III, Chapter 6 uses it as a protective floor in Cat I/II deal-by-deal waterfalls. Disclose this clearly in PPM: 'Incentive fee requires NAV > higher of HWM and Reference Hurdle' — LPs appreciate the guard rail.
